cand.title: University of Toronto Model United Nations 2027
cand.organizationName: University of Toronto Model United Nations

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Verified relevant contacts: Gourav Gupta, Under-Secretary-General External (external@utmun.ca), handles delegation relationships and registration enquiries; Adrian J/Julian Lam, Under-Secretary-General Internal (internal@utmun.ca), is the university-listed primary contact and has conference/venue logistics responsibility. Escalation: Christopher Rhee, Under-Secretary-General Finance (finance@utmun.ca), whose office is the constitutional secondary signing authority; Daisy Zhao, Secretary-General (organization lists sg@utmun.ca). These are relevant organizer contacts, not verified holders of a hotel block or exclusive accommodation purchasing authority.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced activity dates: February 11–14, 2027, University of Toronto St. George Campus, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. Registration is open. The official 2027 committee slate publishes 1,400 delegates; treat this as expected scale, not confirmed registrations. No officially announced 2028 dates or venue were found.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using supplied hotel specifications: realistic fit is a limited visiting-school/chaperone room block, speaker/VIP lodging or a small auxiliary meeting, not exclusive housing or hosting the full 1,400-delegate programme. A 157-room waterfront property can serve a subset only; no evidence establishes 15–109 peak rooms for this event. St. George’s Bloor/College-area campus is north of Queens Quay, so the hotel lacks the campus-adjacent convenience advantage; evaluate transport and February conditions before quoting. This is a city-campus event, not resort demand. No catering, restaurant availability or reception capacity promise should be made before hotel verification.
findings.venueCommitments: Published 2027 venue: University of Toronto St. George Campus, downtown Toronto proper, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The edition-specific venue directory identifies University College (15 King’s College Circle), Convocation Hall (31 King’s College Circle; opening/closing ceremonies), Sidney Smith Hall (100 St. George Street), Bahen Centre (40 St. George Street), and OISE (252 Bloor Street West). These are announced venues, not independently inspected signed contracts. The homepage also mentions New College and Victoria College; use the dedicated venue directory as the more specific operational list and reconfirm final room allocations.
findings.historicalRotation: Evidence supports repeat Toronto/St. George campus hosting, not rotating destinations: 2025 February 6–9; 2026 January 29–February 1; 2027 February 11–14. The university describes a yearly campus conference. Historical 2026 auxiliary venues included the Royal Sonesta hotel for delegate events/panels, Art Gallery of Ontario for the delegate social, and Hart House Great Hall for a staff reception. None establishes 2027 lodging commitments.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2027 lodging pathway remains unknown: no verified named host hotel, room block, housing bureau, hotel RFP, rates, cutoff, or room-night allocation was located. Historical 2025 and 2026 listings state: “This year, we’re happy to offer several hotel partnerships for our attendees to make the most of their stay in Toronto,” referring readers to the partnerships page; that page could not be retrieved. Those listings name no partner hotels. The only specifically identified historical hotel is Royal Sonesta, for 2026 auxiliary events, not a proven sleeping-room block. The current registration page routes “Registration questions, invoicing, accessibility and accommodation requests” to Gourav Gupta; accommodation here is not proof of hotel housing procurement. Faculty Advisors/Head Delegates register schools; their control of hotel bookings must be confirmed.
findings.organizationStructure: University-recognized student group, UTMUN Club, organizing a yearly high-school Model UN conference with University of Toronto student staff. It is not evidenced as a travel-trade intermediary, corporate meeting owner, PCO or DMC. University campus is the event venue; UTMUN is the organizer. No external agency or housing bureau was identified. Do not substitute the Students’ Union as owner based on a third-party directory.
findings.competitiveLimitations: 2026 Royal Sonesta auxiliary-event use demonstrates an incumbent hotel relationship, not exclusivity, open inventory, a 2027 renewal or a room-block commitment. Historical hotel partnerships create possible incumbent competition but the partner roster is unresolved. No sourced sellout, overflow request, displaced rooms or unmet room demand was found. Attendance is not equivalent to overnight demand; local delegates and university staff must not be counted automatically as hotel guests.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Gourav Gupta and Adrian Lam together now. Ask whether visiting delegations book directly or through negotiated partners; request every 2027 hotel name, booking link, allocation, cutoff, exclusivity and any remaining need. Only if unmet demand exists, offer a capped room-only school/chaperone or speaker proposal, subject to hotel availability, youth-group policies and transport viability. Ask Adrian about auxiliary meetings without assuming available catering. Include Christopher Rhee for budget/approval routing, and request an introduction to the next-cycle team if 2027 is committed. Do not quote an event-wide room block.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the upcoming 2027 edition, campus programming is already announced elsewhere. Sleeping-room sourcing and auxiliary-event accessibility are unconfirmed, not open. Registration being open does not establish hotel procurement availability. Approach as a qualification/relationship opportunity, not a confirmed group lead or a displacement proposal.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: documented yearly Toronto campus recurrence and historical hotel partnerships justify developing a future accommodation-partner relationship. A 2028 cycle is plausible but unannounced; do not create dates, venue commitments or room demand for it. Seek future partner-review timing and outgoing-to-incoming secretariat handover rather than assume an annual open RFP.
